title: Nine Dancers, One Dragon — and They Never Touch It | China Travel Expert
description:
Nine dancers lift one dragon up to 70 metres long — and none of them ever touch it. Would you chase the pearl?

In a Chinese dragon dance, the whole body rides on wooden poles — the dancers grip the poles, not the silk. A big ceremonial dragon can take up to fifty people to bring alive, its frame built from lightweight bamboo and silk and stretching anywhere from 25 to 70 metres. Up front, a leader carries a rod topped with a ball — the "Pearl of Wisdom" — and the endless "dragon chasing the pearl" stands for the pursuit of wisdom. The dance goes back to the Han dynasty, when it was a rite to honour ancestors and pray for rain. Tradition says the longer the dragon, the more luck it brings.

🧭 Expert Tip: The best time to catch a real one is Lunar New Year — look for temple fairs (庙会) and lantern festivals, not staged tourist shows.
